title: Results Day
subtitle: The final chapter: Maya takes the IELTS test.
paras: Two years after arriving, Maya decided to apply for a master's degree, which meant taking the IELTS test. Her grammar was accurate and her vocabulary was wide, but she knew from experience that small spelling mistakes could cost her marks. She spent a month on practice papers, learning to analyse each question before writing a single word.

On the morning of the exam she felt surprisingly calm. The listening section went quickly; she checked every answer twice, knowing that a misspelled word would be marked wrong. In the writing section, the essay asked for her opinion on whether universities should teach practical skills. She planned each paragraph carefully and made every sentence earn its place.

Her tutor had told her to emphasise one clear idea and to finish with a conclusion that answered the question directly, so that is exactly what she did. She used linking words such as although and therefore to guide the examiner through her argument, and she tried to persuade rather than simply describe.

Two weeks later, the results arrived. Maya had scored Band 8 overall, with her highest score in the category she had once feared most: writing. She read the email three times before calling her friends. The whole journey — every flat, every job, every presentation — had led to this moment.
discuss: What did Maya do that made the biggest difference to her result? Looking back over all six chapters, which moment in her story would you choose as the turning point?

items.clue: the rules for how words are put together
items.trick: Double M, and it ends in -AR, never -ER.

items.clue: all the words that a person knows
items.trick: Say all five parts: vo-ca-bu-lar-y. It ends in -ARY.

items.clue: knowledge you get from doing things
items.trick: EX + PERI + ENCE: it ends in -ENCE.
A Y in the middle. British -YSE (American: analyze).

items.clue: paying attention to sounds or speech
items.trick: LISTEN keeps its silent T, then -ING. Only one N.

items.clue: putting words on paper or a screen
items.trick: WRITE drops its E and does NOT double the T.

items.clue: a section of writing that begins on a new line
items.trick: PARA + GRAPH. The PH at the end sounds like F.

items.clue: a group of words that expresses a complete thought
items.trick: Three Es and no A: sEntEncE.

items.clue: to show that something is especially important
the final part of an essay
items.trick: CONCLUDE changes its DE to SION.
Only one L at the start, then THOUGH.

items.clue: for that reason; as a result
items.trick: THERE + FORE, with an E at the end.

items.clue: to make someone agree by giving good reasons
items.trick: PER + SUADE: U comes before A.

items.clue: a group of things of the same type
items.trick: An E in the middle, not an A: cat-E-gory.
A silent W: the WHOLE pizza, not a HOLE in it.
